body: Power Blade is an NES action platformer published by Taito, following NOVA through a futuristic computer system seized by aliens. Six sectors hold data tapes needed to reach the central control area. NOVA's weapon is an energy boomerang that can be thrown in eight directions, giving the player useful angles against threats above and below. The mission combines jumping and combat with a search inside each sector. Reaching its end requires finding the person who can provide access to the protected database.

The six sectors can be tackled in a chosen order. Within each one, an agent supplies an identification card that opens the way toward its security room and boss. Collecting the tape after that encounter brings the central objective closer. Power-ups improve the boomerang's range, strength and number of projectiles, while a power suit adds another means of surviving the opposition. The stage becomes a small assignment with several connected tasks, rather than simply a stretch of hazards leading to an exit.

Power Blade substantially reworked the earlier Japanese game Power Blazer. Levels, the hero's appearance and the controls changed, while the agents and multidirectional weapon gave the overseas release a different rhythm. Its North American debut followed in 1991, with a European edition in 1992. Kinuyo Yamashita composed the score, and Mike Winterbauer created the muscular cover illustration. The changes make this an unusually substantial example of localisation: the journey from one region to another also produced a different approach to moving and fighting through a stage.

Find the agent before the security room
A localisation that rebuilt the action
